transcript: Tonight, my friend Tony and I saw Amani at Rattlesnake Theater, co produced by National Black Theater, and I loved it. Amani is the story of a girl who's raised by her father with a strong sense of self assurance and self acceptance. But as she grows up, she learns how hard it can be to navigate her journey of self discovery when the world around her is constantly trying to prescribe an identity onto her. It's a story of black liberation and radical imagination, poignantly illustrated through the metaphor of building oneself a rocket to go to space. Afterwards, they hosted a brief community discussion to make space for processing and reflecting on the show, and it was really cool to hear about the way that the piece connected with audience members in different ways. Amani is running through March 12th, so don't miss it. And with that, another program for my collection.
